C0.quote: select a candidate minimizing the social cost
C0.note: Distortion of deterministic voting rules (veto core) with ordinal input; learning-augmented variants.

C1.quote: The distortion of an algorithm is its worst-case approximation factor
C1.note: Main results are distortion upper/lower bounds and robustness-consistency trade-offs (WD). AL is secondary: algorithm design, no complexity results; included since it designs algorithms, but could be omitted.

C2.1.quote: ALG receives as input a preference profile σ

C2.2.quote: each voter’s list of candidates ranked by distance
C2.2.note: Rankings are strict bijections σ_v though induced from weak distance relation.

C2.3.quote: the distance between a voter and a candidate quantifies how much the voter prefers
C2.3.note: Voters have positions in a metric space and distances (held cardinal attitude).

C2.4.quote: A given instance (V, C, d) induces preference rankings over candidates for each voter.
C2.4.note: Ranking is defined as induced by the metric (the held distances) and the rule is applied to it directly; no statement on submission or reporting.

C3.1.note: No analysis considers misreporting; rankings are induced by the metric.

C3.2.note: No statement that voters submit rankings truthfully; rankings are simply defined as induced by the metric.

C4.1.quote: d is aligned with the preference profile σ
C4.1.note: Cardinal distances/social cost are defined and linked to rankings by alignment (d ▷ σ).

C5.1.quote: The goal is to output a candidate that minimizes the social cost.
C5.1.note: Distortion with respect to social cost is the evaluation criterion.

C5.2.quote: the worst-case multiplicative approximation it achieves to the optimum
C5.2.note: Social cost is evaluated on underlying metric d, defined separately from the ranking input.

VOT.note: Voters are located in space and induce rankings but take no action in the model.

ORG.note: No organiser acting in the model.

DES.note: Designer picks the algorithm and δ, but the designer's choice is analysed as an algorithm's guarantees rather than modelled as an agent with its own objective; coded not present.

C8.1.note: NA: no STRAT or MIXED types.

claims.quote: the designer can achieve a consistency of 2 with a guaranteed robustness of 5.
it is reasonable to assume that the designer may also have access to historical observations
leading to an optimal learning-augmented algorithm guided by a prediction for the optimal candidate.

C9.1.note: Claims concern which algorithm/parameter a designer should choose and relevance to real decisions.

C9.2.note: Applying the guarantees to real elections needs that submitted rankings equal the voters' distance-induced rankings; this is not stated. The link from rankings to metric costs is stated (alignment).

C10.1.note: No statement of a procedural reading.
